circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281-kilometre motorsport facility on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, which has served as the venue for the season-concluding Formula One Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The track represents the second Formula One circuit to be established in the Middle East, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various supporting motorsport competitions. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification, meeting the highest international racing standards.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km motorsport venue that has twice hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across separate periods in Formula One history. Originally called the Österreichring, it held the race for 18 consecutive years beginning in 1970, then resumed hosting the event from 1997 to 2003 following a reconstruction and shortening of the layout.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital city, positioned alongside Baku Boulevard, and at over 6 km it ranks among the longest venues on the Formula One calendar. Following its debut as host of the 2016 European Grand Prix, the circuit established itself as a permanent fixture with the first Azerbaijan Grand Prix in 2017, both events managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Bahrain International Circuit, a 5. 412 km track inaugurated in 2004, hosts the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, which was the first F1 race staged in the Middle East. Beyond its primary F1 role, the venue accommodates various racing series including drag racing, GP2 competition, and 24-hour endurance events, while holding an FIA Grade 1 license with multiple circuit configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test of driver and machine capabilities. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Spa-Francorchamps circuit in Belgium's Wallonia region spans 7. 004 kilometres and has been hosting the Belgian Grand Prix since 1925, featuring in the inaugural 1950 F1 season. The venue has maintained annual Grand Prix races from 1985 onward, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361-kilometre track serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its flagship F1 event, the circuit has accommodated numerous other major motorsport series including sportscar championships and various open-wheel racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Situated in Jiading, the Shanghai International Circuit is a Chinese motorsport venue that hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, with the event resuming from 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing series competitions alongside its return to the Formula One calendar.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located near villages in Northamptonshire, England, is the traditional home of the British Grand Prix, having first staged the race in 1948 and then hosting the inaugural World Championship round in 1950. After alternating venues with Aintree and Brands Hatch for three decades, the British Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, while the circuit also regularly features MotoGP racing.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it debuted in 1986. Built remarkably quickly in just eight months starting in late 1985, the permanent road course was constructed outside the city near a highway rather than as a street circuit through Budapest's largest park as initially proposed.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Monza's 5. 793 km circuit near Milan has hosted Italy's Grand Prix continuously since 1949, missing only the 1980 season for renovations, making it one of the longest-serving Formula One venues. Constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility, the track earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" through its distinctive combination of lengthy straights and swift corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and managed by Honda Mobilityland. Renowned for hosting Formula One and Super Formula racing events, the track accommodates up to 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track winding through Paradise, Nevada, that incorporates the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The layout showcases iconic venues and landmarks including major resort casinos and entertainment destinations, creating a challenging road course through the heart of the city's most recognizable areas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 3 km Mexico City circuit honors two racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both died in motorsport accidents during the 1960s. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across three separate eras, most recently from 2015 onwards under its current "Mexico City Grand Prix" designation, after a 23-year absence from the calendar.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 turns and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track debuted on the Formula One calendar in 2022 and has since hosted the annual Miami Grand Prix, with Formula E adopting a modified version of the course starting in 2025–26.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco, commonly known as Monte Carlo, is a 3. 337 km street circuit that winds through the city streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encircling the harbour of the Principality of Monaco.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km circuit that rejoined the Formula One calendar in 2021 to host the revived Dutch Grand Prix, though this arrangement concluded in 2026. Fans affectionately call it "The Roller coaster in the Dunes" because its winding layout through the dunes features sharply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz combined with dramatic elevation shifts that create an exhilarating driving experience.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a high-speed racing facility situated near Lusail in northern Qatar, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: São Paulo's Interlagos circuit, a 4. 309 km counterclockwise track opened in 1940, was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aviation accident eight years earlier. The venue, which now serves as Pace's burial site, also features a karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, serving as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Formula One since its inaugural 2021 edition. The track has also recently expanded its motorsport calendar to include international electric racing championships.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue located in Singapore that winds through the Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang planning districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing various driving skills. The venue accommodates 140,700 spectators and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP, NASCAR, and endurance racing competitions, while previously accommodating various other racing series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand as his racing nation.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two World Drivers' Championships during his 23-season career with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including multiple Le Mans 24 Hours wins and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both the Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Italy in Formula One, driving for Mercedes since his 2025 debut. The driver claimed the world championship title in 2026 at the youngest age in the sport's history, accumulating nine race victories along the way.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who races for the Haas team in Formula One.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas is a Finnish driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One. He has achieved two championship runner-up finishes during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, and has claimed 10 race victories over his 13-season career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian endurance racing driver competing in the LMP2 category with AF Corse in the Asian Le Mans Series, following prior stints in the European series. He holds a reserve driver position with Haas while having made seven Formula One race starts across the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly races for Alpine in Formula One, having previously achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver racing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who shares the record for most championship titles with seven victories. The driver holds multiple records within the sport, including the most race wins, pole positions, and podium appearances across his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing extensive racing experience from multiple disciplines. Beyond his F1 career, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, notably securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc is a Monégasque driver currently competing for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has secured nine race victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver K-Mag has competed across multiple racing series, including two separate stints in Formula One between 2014 and 2024. Currently, he races in the world endurance championship as a factory driver for BMW with the WRT team.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British driver who secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 14 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon recently drove for Haas in Formula One after previously achieving his sole victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while racing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons of competition. He finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has claimed eight Grand Prix victories during his Formula One tenure with Mercedes, competing across eight different seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz Jr. is a Spanish Formula One driver currently racing for Williams. Over his 12-season career in the sport, he has secured four Grand Prix victories.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who previously spent two seasons in Formula One, from 2023 to 2024. He has now transitioned to endurance racing, competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with Ford after earlier racing in the LMGT3 category for Proton Competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently competing for Aston Martin in the sport's top tier.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. He competed as a full-time driver throughout 2021-2025 before transitioning to a reserve position in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, Verstappen has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the series between 2022 and 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, serving as Renault's official Formula One entry until the manufacturer's withdrawal at the end of 2025. Previously operating under the Renault F1 Team banner, the outfit was rebranded to showcase the French company's Alpine sports car division while maintaining its works team status throughout this period.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has engaged in Formula One competition through multiple team structures, with the current iteration operating under AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari in Formula One competition. As the sport's longest-running and most accomplished team, it has maintained an unbroken presence in the World Championship since its inception in 1950, earning its celebrated nickname from the iconic horse emblem on its vehicles.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR entrepreneur Gene Haas, the team commenced competitive operations in 2016 with a focus on cost-efficient racing strategies. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal position following Guenther Steiner's departure after nearly a decade in the role.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm initially competed in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993, where it operated as an independent constructor for over three decades. The team secured two world championships in sports car racing and won the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours before exiting Formula One in 2025 as the fourth-longest-competing constructor by race entries. Audi AG acquired the organization in 2024 to establish the technical and competitive foundation for its own Formula One program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One competitor headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking, Surrey. Operated as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, the team is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with their current team, Mercedes-AMG Petronas, operating from Brackley under a German licence. The squad adopted a tri-ownership structure in 2022 involving Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in equal partnership. The marque carries the historic "Silver Arrows" moniker, reflecting its storied racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as Red Bull's second team. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the squad operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team structure in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team that commenced operations in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned constructors alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates under the ownership of Austrian conglomerate Red Bull GmbH.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by the Red Bull conglomerate, which also operates Racing Bulls in the championship. Founded in 2005 and led by Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, the team is now directed by Laurent Mekies.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Atlassian Williams F1 Team, a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerged following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Based at Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has established itself as a significant force in the sport's history.
